funding: State museum under the Ministry of Culture. The 2026 €50M revamp is funded half by ticket sales and half by ministry funds. Private gifts include Veronica Atkins (about €4.5M, Boboli amphitheatre, 2023), the Edwin L. Wiegand Foundation ($1M, Vasari Corridor, Oct 2023) and Ferragamo (€600k, 2014).
why_flagged: Unions protested in March–April 2026 over long-serving temporary staff losing jobs under the outsourced CoopCulture services contract.
other_findings: On 5 April 2026 museum workers backed by Sudd Cobas protested in front of Botticelli's Venus over precarious jobs (Open, 6 Apr 2026).
Dire (31 Mar 2026) names the services contractor as CoopCulture; workers say it did not keep earlier agreements after the contract changed hands.
Unverified: the unions USB and Sudd Cobas say CoopCulture and the ministry use on-call contracts (union claim, reported by Dire).
Ultima Generazione climate activists protested at Primavera on 22 July 2022 and at the Venus on 13 Feb 2024; neither protest named a Uffizi funder.
bottom_line: A state museum funded by the Ministry of Culture and ticket sales, with large private gifts from US patrons and Florentine companies. No reporting found of controversial funders. The one issue worth watching is labour: the dispute over outsourced staff working under the CoopCulture contract.

funding: Endowment ($60.8M) plus private gifts. In FY2025, 1,387 donors gave $4.83M; total contributed revenue was $12.38M and expenses $16.83M. The Amon G. Carter Foundation and Walton Family Foundation ($20M endowment, 2017) are major funders; public grants come from the City of Fort Worth, Arts Fort Worth, Fort Worth Tourism PID and the Texas Commission on the Arts.
why_flagged: In October 2024 the museum closed its Cowboy exhibition for about two weeks and reopened it with a mature-content warning, which artist rafa esparza called censorship.
other_findings: Cowboy opened 28 Sept 2024, closed for about two weeks by 11 October, and reopened with a mature-content sign; the museum said it needed time to decide how to communicate with visitors (Dallas Voice, an LGBTQ outlet).
Artist rafa esparza said: "I see this as a form of censorship" (Dallas Voice).
funders: Fort Worth Tourism Public Improvement District
bottom_line: A free museum funded mostly by its endowment and by local foundations and individuals. The founder's foundation is still a top donor. No reporting found of controversial funders. The one issue on record is the 2024 Cowboy closure, which an artist called censorship.

funding: Municipal museum funded by the City of Ghent; under an agreement approved in May 2026, Flanders takes over its structural operating subsidy (freeing over €3M a year for Ghent) and it becomes a Flemish museum on 1 January 2029. Corporate partners include ENGIE, which has funded youth art workshops since 2012.
why_flagged: Energy company ENGIE has sponsored S.M.A.K.'s youth art workshops since 2012.
other_findings: ENGIE, with the ENGIE Foundation and CLW Ghent, has supported S.M.A.K. art workshops for young people since 2012; the partnership took third place at the Belgian sponsorship awards (S.M.A.K., 19 Dec 2021).
bottom_line: A publicly funded museum moving from city to Flemish government funding by 2029. The only flagged sponsor is ENGIE's long-running support for youth workshops. Worth watching: the transfer and the takeover of the M HKA collection.
